16 An aircraft travels at a constant velocity of 90 m s–1 in horizontal flight. The diagram shows some
of the forces acting on the aircraft.
drag
2400 N
thrust
weight
The mass of the aircraft is 2000 kg.
What is the power produced by the thrust force?
A
1.8 × 105
W
B
2.2 × 105
W
C
1.8 × 106
W
D
2.0 × 106
W

hints: Notice the aircraft is in horizontal flight at constant velocity of $90 \text{ m s}^{-1}$, so the horizontal forces must balance and the $2400 \text{ N}$ drag tells you the thrust.
Recall power for a force parallel to motion is $P = Fv$, where $F$ must be the forward thrust in $\text{N}$ and $v$ is $90 \text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Check why the $2000 \text{ kg}$ mass and vertical weight do not enter the thrust power calculation, then multiply $2400 \text{ N}$ by $90 \text{ m s}^{-1}$.
walkthrough: Constant velocity means zero resultant force. Horizontally, forward thrust must exactly balance backward drag shown as $2400 \text{ N}$, so $F_{thrust} = 2400 \text{ N}$.
Power produced by a force along the direction of motion is $P = Fv$. Thrust is parallel to the $90 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ velocity, so it does work at rate $F_{thrust}v$.
Substitute with units: $P = 2400 \text{ N} \times 90 \text{ m s}^{-1} = 216000 \text{ W}$.
Weight acts vertically downwards while displacement is horizontal, so it contributes zero power and the $2000 \text{ kg}$ mass is not needed except to find weight.
Round $2.16 \times 10^5 \text{ W}$ to the given precision as $2.2 \times 10^5 \text{ W}$. This is option B.

A.explanation: Uses $2000 \times 90$ with mass in $\text{kg}$ as if it were a force in $\text{N}$, giving $1.8 \times 10^5 \text{ W}$.

B.explanation: Thrust equals drag at constant velocity, so $P = 2400 \times 90 = 2.16 \times 10^5 \text{ W}$.

C.explanation: Uses weight $\approx 20000 \text{ N}$ times $90 \text{ m s}^{-1}$, but weight acts vertically and does no work in horizontal flight.

D.explanation: Is about ten times too large and does not equal thrust $\times$ velocity for the given $2400 \text{ N}$ drag.
